hook.text: We say 'passed away' instead of 'died' and 'restroom' instead of 'toilet.'

buildup.text: Euphemisms are mild words that replace ones considered harsh, rude, or uncomfortable.

discovery.text: Taboo words trigger real physiological responses—increased heart rate and skin conductance.

twist.text: Euphemisms wear out: 'toilet' was itself a euphemism for an earlier term that felt too blunt.

climax.text: This 'euphemism treadmill' means every replacement eventually becomes the new taboo word.

punchline.text: We keep renaming the uncomfortable—it never stays polite.
